articles.title: Zelda Sandoval, 96, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Zelda Sandoval for the many years of service to Cedar Hollow.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Kettle Hill Block Association in his or her name. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Cedar Hollow.

Born in Cedar Hollow in the years after the war, Zelda Sandoval spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Zelda Sandoval died in April at home on Vine Street, at the age of 96.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to the Marsh Landing Pond Committee
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the March meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

Please keep the community garden in the budget. Many of us on Canton Terrace use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Canton Terrace for 32 years, and I want to say what a difference the Marsh Landing Pond Committee has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the March meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Margaret Garrity, Upper Commons

articles.title: Council Tables Pet Adoption Fair Ordinance
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Ridge Lane disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Public works estimates the work will take about 35 weeks once it starts in September.
Residents of Tannery Flats said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: The Upper Commons Historical Society Opens Sidewalk Ramp on Ridge Street
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 38 weeks and will be paid for with $25,000 raised locally.
body: The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Several residents on Ridge Street said they had been waiting since 1994 for something like this. The effort began in October when a handful of neighbors met at the Kettle Hill Park gate to talk about sidewalk ramp.

Keith Bachman, who has lived on Ridge Street for 38 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Kettle Hill Park gate on Sunday at 7 p.m.

articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. A 2005 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Birch Avenue from the corner of Adams Place.
